candidates.source_name: IMF Kosovo country page (Article IV, program reviews, staff reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Primary analytic source on Kosovo's banking and payment system: Article IV staff reports, selected issues papers, SBA/RSF review documents. Discusses credit-to-GDP, NPLs, supervision gaps, crisis management and payment-system modernisation with frankness domestic sources avoid. 2026 Article IV concluded; 2024 Article IV concluded alongside 3rd SBA/RSF reviews.
candidates.legal_status: public, IMF copyright with permitted quotation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of country page + /en/publications/cr filtered by country code UVK; PDF download and text extraction; watch PR/CS press-release feeds for staff-level agreements
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from press releases to CR series
queries_used: IMF Kosovo Article IV staff report banking sector financial system

candidates.source_name: IMF Kosovo Financial Sector Stability Review (FSSR) technical assistance report
candidates.why_relevant: FSAP-equivalent deep dive for a non-FSAP-mandatory jurisdiction: supervision, systemic risk oversight, crisis management, financial safety net, and payment/settlement infrastructure. Highest-density single document on Kosovo banking-system weaknesses. Notably, CBK republishes it in Serbian, giving a bilingual terminology anchor.
candidates.access_status: open (eLibrary may throttle bulk PDF access)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct PDF fetch; mirror the CBK-hosted SRB/ALB language versions as fallback if eLibrary blocks
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query; snowballed to CBK-hosted translation via Serbian-language query
queries_used: IMF Kosovo Article IV staff report banking sector financial system

candidates.source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Kosovo (country code XK) financial sector documents
candidates.why_relevant: Holds Kosovo Financial Sector Assessment, ROSC accounting/auditing updates, Financial Sector Strengthening Project appraisal/implementation docs, Public Finance Review, and Country Partnership Framework reviews (e.g. Report No. 167914-XK). Project documents often disclose bank-level and supervisory detail not otherwise published.
candidates.legal_status: public, CC-BY on most Open Knowledge items
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the Documents & Reports API (docs API v2) with country=Kosovo and majdocType filters; harvest PDF/TXT variants (both are served)
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball across document series
queries_used: World Bank Kosovo Financial Sector Assessment FSAP report

candidates.source_name: World Bank Kosovo documents in Serbian (Srpski) — e.g. Kosovo Pregled javnih finansija
candidates.why_relevant: Confirms the World Bank publishes Kosovo material in local languages; these translations are the cleanest bilingual glossary for financial-sector terminology (bankarski sektor, nekvalitetni krediti/NPL, adekvatnost kapitala) used later in sr-language searching of bank disclosures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Filter Documents & Reports API by language=Serbian / Albanian; use as translation-layer corpus

candidates.source_name: Agjencia e Statistikave të Kosovës (ASK) — Kosovo Agency of Statistics
candidates.why_relevant: National statistical authority (askdata portal, business registry statistics, national accounts, prices, ICT usage). Does NOT own monetary/financial statistics — those sit with CBK — but supplies the denominators (GDP, enterprise counts, household ICT/payment-adjacent indicators) needed to normalise banking and payments series. Publishes sq/sr/en.
candidates.access_status: open; askdata PxWeb-style portal likely offers API/CSV export
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest askdata cubes via PxWeb/JSON-stat endpoints; scheduled monthly poll of publication calendar
queries_used: Agjencia e Statistikave të Kosovës ASK statistika financiare bankat

candidates.source_name: BQK/CBK statistics hub (Rreth statistikave) — national aggregator of bank-level returns
candidates.why_relevant: The de-facto aggregator for Kosovo banking data: monetary & financial statistics and external-sector statistics are legally CBK's responsibility, compiled from commercial banks, MFIs, insurers and pension funds. Underlies every IMF/World Bank Kosovo series, so it is the upstream node for the whole aggregator layer.
candidates.access_status: open; site serves sq/sr/en via ?lang= parameter
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl time-series tables and the ?lang=sq|sr|en variants; store all three language editions of each PDF for the translation layer
candidates.discovered_via_method: Albanian-language search; snowball from ASK query

candidates.why_relevant: Serial with numbered editions (No. 20, No. 21) published in Albanian, Serbian and English under stable wp-content paths — a predictable, machine-harvestable archive and the best bilingual anchor for stability/risk terminology.

candidates.source_name: BQK CBK Annual Reports archive (Raporti Vjetor) — historical PDF series
candidates.why_relevant: Continuous annual series back to ~2009 with sector-level balance sheets, licensed-institution lists and payment-system statistics. Critically, the site was re-platformed: older files sit under /repository/docs/... and newer ones under /wp-content/uploads/2024/11/..., so pre-migration URLs are exactly the class of link that needs web-archive recovery.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl archive index; for any 404 on legacy /repository/docs paths, fall back to Wayback CDX lookup rather than marking dead
queries_used: "web.archive.org" Kosovo bank annual report raporti vjetor pdf

candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine + CDX API (recovery layer for removed Kosovo bank/IR disclosures)
candidates.why_relevant: The only practical way to recover Kosovo bank IR pages, quarterly disclosures and pre-migration BQK PDFs after site redesigns (bqk-kos.org moved from /repository/docs to /wp-content; commercial banks routinely rotate 'Raporte financiare' pages). CDX API enables systematic diffing of what a bank used to publish versus what it publishes now.
candidates.legal_status: archive copies; respect IA terms and exclusion requests
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CDX queries per bank domain with url=<domain>/*&filter=mimetype:application/pdf&collapse=urlkey; also Save Page Now on every live disclosure URL at first sighting to guarantee future recoverability
queries_used: "web.archive.org" Kosovo bank annual report raporti vjetor pdf

candidates.source_name: archive.today / archive.ph mirror
candidates.why_relevant: Secondary web archive that captures JS-heavy pages and press releases the Wayback Machine misses, and is often the only surviving copy of deleted Kosovo bank news posts. Complementary redundancy for the archive layer.

candidates.legal_status: third-party archive; grey area, use for verification not redistribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-volume lookups only; treat 403 as bot defence, not death

candidates.legal_status: proprietary; headline ratings quotable, full reports licensed

negative_findings.description: Searching in Albanian for 'Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës' (Kosovo Banking Association, SHBK/KBA) returned no association website or association-published statistics in the result set; results redirected entirely to BQK/CBK pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed URL for a Kosovo banking association aggregator this run. The actor is widely referenced in the sector, so absence is a search-coverage failure, not proof of non-existence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A national banking association is the classic private-sector aggregator of member-bank data and press releases and would be a high-value node in this cell.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found that S&P Global Ratings or Moody's assigns a sovereign rating to Kosovo; Fitch's April assignment was reported as Kosovo's first-ever sovereign rating and the country was previously the only Western Balkans state without one.
negative_findings.result_summary: Rating-agency coverage of Kosovo appears effectively single-source (Fitch), with Scope Ratings unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Single-agency coverage means no cross-agency triangulation on sovereign or bank credit views; the aggregator layer must lean harder on IMF/EBRD/EC analysis.

negative_findings.description: No full Kosovo FSAP was located. Kosovo had a 2012 FSAP and a 2020 IMF stocktaking of its recommendations, plus a Financial Sector Stability Review; Kosovo does not appear among mandatory-FSAP jurisdictions.
negative_findings.result_summary: FSAP material for Kosovo is sparse and dated; the FSSR is the practical substitute.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts expecting an FSAP-grade assessment must substitute the FSSR plus Article IV annexes, and should not assume FSAP-standard coverage of payment-system oversight.

negative_findings.description: ASK (Kosovo Agency of Statistics) does not produce monetary/financial or banking statistics; those responsibilities sit legally with BQK/CBK, with commercial banks and other financial corporations as reporting units.
negative_findings.result_summary: Targeting ASK for banking data is a dead end by design; ASK supplies macro denominators only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort and mis-attribution of banking series to the statistical agency.

negative_findings.description: No Serbian- or Albanian-language term was found this run for the web-archiving concept as applied to Kosovo bank disclosures; Serbian and Albanian queries surfaced no local-language archiving initiative or national web archive for the .rks-gov.net / Kosovo domain space.
negative_findings.result_summary: The archive layer for Kosovo appears entirely foreign-operated (Internet Archive, archive.today).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no domestic legal-deposit web archive to fall back on; if the Internet Archive misses a capture, the document is likely irrecoverable — argues for proactive Save Page Now on every disclosure URL.

negative_findings.description: Fitch Ratings and IMF eLibrary were not fetched directly this run; registration walls and PDF throttling are assumed from general behaviour, not observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Access status for both is a hypothesis pending the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Do not classify either as blocked or dead on a single failed fetch during verification.

coverage_gaps.description: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) not located; also unconfirmed: an insurance/microfinance association (AMIK) and a Kosovo payments/fintech industry body.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted queries for 'Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës', 'Kosovo Banking Association', 'Asociacioni i Institucioneve Mikrofinanciare të Kosovës (AMIK)' and check BQK's licensed-institution and stakeholder pages for outbound association links.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial macro/financial data aggregators (CEIC, Haver, Refinitiv, S&P Capital IQ, Moody's Analytics BankFocus/Orbis Bank Focus, Fitch Connect) were not evaluated for Kosovo bank-level coverage this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess BankFocus/Orbis and Fitch Connect specifically for whether they carry Kosovo bank financial statements — these are the only realistic sources of standardised bank-level panel data for XK.

coverage_gaps.description: Open statistical data portals were named but not endpoint-mapped: World Bank Global Financial Development Database and WDI, IMF FSI/IFS/CPIS data portals, and ASK's askdata cube API for Kosovo (XK/UVK country codes differ across systems).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map the exact country code per portal (World Bank XKX, IMF UVK/967) and record API endpoints for FSI and GFDD series so banking indicators can be pulled programmatically.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-bank domain inventory was built for Wayback CDX diffing; without a list of Kosovo commercial bank domains (Raiffeisen, ProCredit, NLB, TEB, BKT, BPB, Banka Ekonomike, Ziraat) the archive recovery layer cannot be operationalised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the domain list from BQK's licensed-banks register and Wikipedia's List of banks in Kosovo, then run CDX PDF enumeration per domain and Save-Page-Now every live disclosure URL.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language coverage was satisfied mainly through CBK's own ?lang=sr translations and one World Bank Serbian PDF; no independent Serbian-language aggregator or archive covering Kosovo's financial sector (e.g. Serbian-language media or NBS-adjacent commentary on north-Kosovo banking) was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Serbian-language sources on north-Kosovo banking and the euro/dinar payment regulation dispute, which is a payments-relevant topic likely covered only in sr.

brief: Kosovo's aggregator and translation layer is dominated by international institutions rather than domestic ones: the IMF (Article IV series plus a Financial Sector Stability Review that substitutes for the absent modern FSAP), the World Bank documents repository, EBRD Transition Report country assessments, and the European Commission enlargement package together supply nearly all analytically frank commentary on the banking and payment system. Domestically, BQK/CBK — not the statistics agency ASK — is the legal owner and de-facto aggregator of monetary and financial statistics, and it usefully publishes each report in Albanian, Serbian and English under predictable URL patterns, making it the sector's best built-in translation layer alongside the BIS speech archive. Third-party credit assessment is effectively single-source: Fitch alone rates the sovereign (BB-, stable) and some Kosovo banks, with free rating detail reachable mainly through mirrors such as Cbonds and SeeNews. The archive layer is entirely foreign-operated — the Internet Archive CDX API is the only systematic route to recovering pre-migration BQK PDFs and lapsed bank IR pages, and with no domestic legal-deposit web archive, proactive Save Page Now capture of every disclosure URL is a necessity rather than an optimisation.
